name: olv1items
description: Open LLM Leaderboard v1 item-level correctness from tinyBenchmarks (Maia Polo et al., 2024) for 395 models on 62 tasks (57 MMLU subjects, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, TruthfulQA, Winogrande, GSM8K); task score = mean item score.

license.note: Item scores are model outputs on public benchmarks, produced by the Open LLM Leaderboard (Hugging Face) and redistributed by tinyBenchmarks under MIT; benchmark questions are not redistributed here (their own licenses apply to them).  The leaderboard results and details datasets declare no license on their cards; the requests dataset is apache-2.0.  Keep the MIT notice above with any copy of the item data.

matrix.model_order: sorted by HF id with Python str ordering (code points)
matrix.benchmark_order: 57 MMLU subjects alphabetical (= mmlu.matrix.npz), then arc_challenge, hellaswag, truthfulqa_mc2, winogrande, gsm8k
matrix.score: binary tasks: count_correct / n_items (exact); truthfulqa_mc2: float64 mean of per-item mc2

layout.task_offsets: (63,) items of task k are rows task_offsets[k]:task_offsets[k+1]
layout.correct_bits: (n_items, 50) uint8 = np.packbits(correct, axis=1, bitorder='big'); zero rows for non-binary items

items.decode: S = np.unpackbits(z['correct_bits'], axis=1, count=int(z['n_models']), bitorder='big').astype(float); S[z['float_item_index']] = z['float_scores']  # (n_items, n_models); or build_olv1items.load_item_scores(path)
items.item_identity: The source has no question ids or text: an item is identified by its row in lb.pickle (the example order of the leaderboard details files used by tinyBenchmarks).

pickle_safety.method: static scan with pickletools.genops (no code executed); then pickle.Unpickler with find_class restricted to the globals found by the scan that are also in the allowlist

allowlist_extensions.numpy._core.numeric._frombuffer: numpy's rebuild function for arrays pickled with protocol 5 (ndarray.__reduce_ex__(5)): frombuffer(buf, dtype).reshape(shape); it only views a byte buffer as a non-object array.  Mapped to _frombuffer_guarded, which also refuses object dtypes.
allowlist_extensions.numpy.core.numeric._frombuffer: numpy's rebuild function for arrays pickled with protocol 5 (ndarray.__reduce_ex__(5)): frombuffer(buf, dtype).reshape(shape); it only views a byte buffer as a non-object array.  Mapped to _frombuffer_guarded, which also refuses object dtypes.

pickle_safety.post_load_validation: top level {'data','models'}; models list[str]; every task {'correctness': 2-D float64 ndarray, n_models columns}

mmlu_matrix.note: data/mmlu.matrix.npz (download_mmlu.py) reads acc_norm, falling back to acc, from the last results file of each model; olv1items reproduces acc of the run whose details tinyBenchmarks used.  Outlier models differ because mmlu.matrix took a later re-evaluation (mmlu_matrix_agrees_with).

official_v1_results.note: per task: models whose task score equals the official aggregate (metric column) of at least one of their results files

caveats: TruthfulQA items are continuous mc2 values, not 0/1; item-level selection that assumes Bernoulli items must treat truthfulqa_mc2 separately.
Total items = 28659 (MMLU 14,042 + ARC 1,172 + HellaSwag 10,042 + TruthfulQA 817 + Winogrande 1,267 + GSM8K 1,319); 395 x 62 = 24490 is the number of model-task cells, not items.
Items carry no question ids/text in the source; ids are lb.pickle row indices.
The 395 models are the tinyBenchmarks selection of leaderboard v1 models evaluated 2023-07..2024-01, not a random sample of the leaderboard.

For 2 model(s) (CHIH-HUNG/llama-2-13b-huangyt_FINETUNE2_3w, CHIH-HUNG/llama-2-13b-huangyt_Fintune_1_17w-q_k_v_o_proj) open-llm-leaderboard-old/results holds only the late-2023 winogrande/gsm8k re-run; the aggregate results file of their original run was taken from their details repo at a pinned commit (primary_results_source = 'details_repo'), so their other 60 tasks are checked against official values and eval_timestamp/eval_date date the original run.

For 176 models winogrande and gsm8k come from the leaderboard's late-2023 re-run (tasks_from_other_results_file); eval_timestamp/eval_date refer to the run that produced the remaining tasks (primary_results_file).  For 63 of them the re-run's model_sha differs from the primary run's.

request.submitted_time is later than eval_timestamp for 179 models: request files are keyed by model+precision and re-submissions overwrite them, so use eval_date as the model date for temporal splits.
request.model_type is free text from the leaderboard; model_type_norm maps it to pretrained / fine-tuned / instruction-tuned / RL-tuned (None if unknown).
